nodes.title: Description
widgets_values:
Loads and configures the Qwen Image Edit model for pose transfer:

GGUF Model: Qwen-Image-Edit
LoRA: 4-step Lightning adapter to speed up our model
Model Sampling (3): AuraFlow sampling for increased quality
CFG Norm (1): Normalizes CFG
VAE: Qwen's specialized VAE for encoding/decoding
CLIP: Qwen 2.5 VL text encoder (fp8) for prompt understanding

nodes.title: Description
widgets_values:
Hypothetically, the only area the user needs to mess with. 
Upload your character model.
Update the pose description with a short blurb of what our character is doing.
Input the target height of this sprite. 
Update the path to our list of poses.
Save the image. 

The resulting image should be ready to import into Aesprite to generate a sprite sheet.

Import all the images and then set the color mode to indexed

nodes.title: Description
widgets_values:
Performs the actual pose transfer using Qwen's image editing:

Input Images: Character reference (image 1), pose reference (image 2) from batch folder, background (image 3) 
Text Encoding: Positive prompt (pose instructions) and negative prompt (unwanted elements like backgrounds)
VAE Encode: Converts input image to latent space at 1024x1024
KSampler: Generates new pose using 4 steps, euler sampler, CFG for prompt influence
VAE Decode: Converts latent back to image


Best sampler settings:
4 steps / res_multistep / beta / 1 cfg / 1 denoise

4 steps / euler / simple / 1 cfg / 1 denoise

Learnings:
CFG above 1.2 messes with the pose. 
Denoise below .9 gets wonky.

nodes.title: Description
widgets_values:
Qwen edit can't help itself from adding a shadow no matter how hard you prompt it not to. This part of the workflow removes the background, which should include the shadow, and pastes our image onto our background image. 
It also goes ahead and crops the character to its exact size to to be scaled later.

If the character's color is a close match to the shadow, you may need to try a different model. isnet-anime sometimes works.

nodes.title: Description
widgets_values:
This is the pixel art magic. By using both a Pixel Art SDXL Lora and a Pixelate VAE, we achieve a very nice looking pixelated image. 

We use the base SD model and a super low denoise so that our original image is not edited at all.

nodes.title: Description
widgets_values: Here we down scale our image by 1/8 and then re-upscale it by 8x to create an even more pixelated image. And then we finally downscale our image to our desired height set in the user actions to the left and remove the background, if desired.

Here is where you select your pose or poses. You have four methods. 
If you are generating a batch of sprites, you'll want to load a folder and cycle through the poses or skeletons.
If you have a folder of pose skeletons, input the path to that folder and select index 0 in the format. 
If you have a folder of just poses that still need to be parsed into skeletons, input the poses folder path and select index 2.
If you just want to upload a single pose or skeleton, use the proper loader and select the index.
This is just a bunch of conditionals for deciding which pose to send our prompt and whether or not to run our pose through OpenPose (if it is not already a skeleton).
